lessons.text: When a clause specifies a group of individuals with a condition such as 'covered under any other statutory social security schemes', do not write a rule for that condition.
lessons.applies_when: the clause mentions coverage under other schemes
lessons.review_note: Wrong: C03's reviewed rules exclude NPS, ESIC and EPFO members (three eq false rules).

lessons.text: When a clause states that the applicant must be a specific type of professional or individual, such as 'an Indian scientist working in agriculture', write a rule that confirms their professional status without adding unnecessary conditions.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies a professional requirement

lessons.text: A clause asking for a document, certificate or letter ("No Objection Certificate", "letter of acceptance") is something to submit: write no rule for it.
lessons.applies_when: the clause mentions a document requirement

lessons.text: When a clause specifies that an applicant must be the only girl child in the family, write a rule that checks if the applicant is a woman or girl.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies 'only girl child in the family'
lessons.review_note: Wrong and specific: C15 needs is_only_child, not only a gender check.

lessons.text: When a clause says only one person per family can benefit, write family_member_already_beneficiary eq false.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies 'only one person in the family'

lessons.text: When a benefit can be had only once ("eligible only once", "can be availed only once"), write a has_availed_<scheme>_before eq false rule.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies 'eligible only once during the course of study'

lessons.text: For former or present Ministers, MPs, MLAs, Mayors or District Panchayat chairpersons, use is_former_or_present_listed_political_office_holder when the clause is about the applicant, and family_has_former_or_present_listed_political_office_holder when it is about any family member.
lessons.applies_when: the clause mentions political office holders.

lessons.text: When a clause refers to total income, use 'annual_family_income' instead of 'annual_income'.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies total income from all sources.
lessons.review_note: Not general: C16 uses family income because of an official-source answer; C31's limit is applicant and spouse.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies eligibility based on gender for women scientists, use 'is_woman_or_girl' instead of 'is_permanent_employee'.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies eligibility for women scientists.
lessons.review_note: Doesn't follow from the error (C25's category field).

lessons.text: When a scheme specifies 'any' for eligibility, write the rule with 'or_conditions' to reflect that multiple conditions can be satisfied. If it specifies 'all', write the rule without 'or_conditions', indicating all conditions must be met.
lessons.applies_when: the clause indicates eligibility based on 'any' or 'all'.
flags: no specific keyword left, so it would be sent for every scheme
lessons.review_note: Confuses rule_logic (how rules combine) with or_conditions (alternatives inside one rule).

lessons.text: An age relaxation of X years for named groups is two rules: age lte (limit + X); and age lte limit with or_conditions for each relaxed group (social_category in [...], is_woman_or_girl eq true, has_disability eq true).

When a clause lists several qualifying kinds of one requirement joined by EITHER/OR (courses, years of study, posts), write one rule for that requirement (a yes/no field, or field in [the kinds]), not one rule per kind.
"BPL OR income up to Rs N" is one rule: household_below_bpl eq true, with or_conditions [annual_family_income lte N].
lessons.applies_when: BPL families or income limit is mentioned

lessons.text: When a clause states that an applicant 'must not exceed' a certain limit, write the rule with 'lte' using the specified limit. If it states 'must exceed', write 'gt' instead.
lessons.applies_when: a limit is phrased as 'must not exceed' or 'must exceed'.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies a category or list of eligible conditions, ensure all specified conditions are included in the rule. If the clause lists multiple categories, write a rule that includes all of them.
lessons.applies_when: a clause lists multiple categories or conditions for eligibility.
lessons.review_note: Vague; L012 covers the useful part.

lessons.text: An exclusion clause (excl-, or "is not eligible") names who is excluded, so its rule requires the opposite: field eq false.
lessons.applies_when: a clause states that something is 'not eligible'.
